text:
Jake Evans scored twice for Montreal, and one of them came shorthanded in the second period, a wrist shot that put the Canadiens ahead 2-1 and changed the night at the United Center. Chicago had opened the scoring on a Connor Bedard snap shot four minutes in, but Evans tied it late in the first and then took the lead on the penalty kill. He finished with a goal-and-assist line that included a helper on Kaiden Guhle's goal.

Montreal's 4-1 win was also earned on the ice. The Canadiens had 53 shot attempts to Chicago's 40, and in expected goals (a measure of the quality of chances) they led 2.85 to 2.16. By the deserved-to-win measure, which is the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, Montreal came out ahead 58 percent to 42. They had the better of each period, and the gap was widest in the second. Chicago went 0 for 5 on the power play, though those chances were worth 0.87 expected goals, more than Montreal's three chances produced.

Goaltending tilted it further. Jacob Fowler stopped 20 of 21 shots and saved about 1.2 goals more than the chances against him should have allowed, while Spencer Knight stopped 24 of 27 and finished slightly below expectation. Guhle's goal late in the second came on a chance worth under one percent, and Mike Matheson added an empty-looking cushion with a third-period snap shot. The facts supplied include no records or streaks, so nothing more can be said about where the result leaves either team.
